answer: Prism Vertex Quota. Each agent occupies one vertex in a directed transaction prism, and its influence is capped by the diversity of distinct quartz clusters reachable within two hops. To mint a new vertex, an attacker must first route real volume through independent existing clusters, paying settlement fees and latency on every edge. Sybils sharing upstream paths collapse into one cluster and inherit no extra quota, so each fake identity costs a full independent routing history.
